description: Wisconsin CDL items taken from the May 2026 Commercial Driver's Manual. Federal baseline questions stay in core_cdl.json.

questions.q: A combination vehicle needs a Class A CDL when its GCWR is over 26,000 pounds and the towed unit is:
options: Any trailer, including a small utility trailer
questions.explanation: Class A is a combination over 26,000 pounds that includes a towed unit over 10,000 pounds.

questions.q: A heavy straight truck with a GVWR over 26,000 pounds, and no trailer over 10,000 pounds, requires:
questions.explanation: Class B is a heavy straight vehicle over 26,000 pounds.

questions.q: Which vehicle needs a Class C CDL even though it weighs 26,000 pounds or less?
options: A pickup towing a small boat
A vehicle built to carry 16+ people
A farm tractor used only in a field
A car with a roof cargo box
questions.explanation: Class C covers a small vehicle that carries 16 or more people including the driver, or any size vehicle hauling hazardous materials that require a placard.

questions.q: The GCWR is over 26,000 pounds. The power unit is under 26,000 pounds, and the trailer is over 10,000 pounds. Which class is required?
options: No CDL, because the power unit is under 26,000 pounds
questions.explanation: The Wisconsin class chart still calls that combination Class A when the combination is over 26,000 pounds and the trailer is over 10,000 pounds.

questions.q: Which endorsement is required to tow double or triple trailers?
questions.explanation: T is the doubles and triples endorsement. H is hazardous materials, N is tank, and P is passenger.

questions.q: A passenger endorsement (P) is required for a vehicle designed to transport:
options: 8 or more people including the driver
12 or more people including the driver
16 or more people including the driver
20 or more people including the driver
questions.explanation: P covers a vehicle designed to transport, or actually transporting, 16 or more passengers including the driver. It requires a knowledge test and a skills test.

questions.q: What does restriction L mean on a Wisconsin CDL?
options: No cargo in a tank vehicle
questions.explanation: L means you did not pass the air-brake tests, so you may not operate a commercial vehicle with air brakes.

questions.q: The low-air warning must come on before tank pressure falls below:
questions.explanation: A warning you can see must come on before pressure falls below 60 psi, or one half the governor cut-out pressure on older vehicles. Large buses often warn at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.q: Below 40 mph, a good following-distance rule for a commercial vehicle is at least:
options: One second for each 10 feet of vehicle length
Two seconds total, whatever the length
One car length for each 10 mph
questions.explanation: Keep at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length under 40 mph. Add one more second at higher speeds.

questions.q: A Wisconsin farmer may drive a farm CMV without a CDL only when the trip stays within:
options: 150 miles of a farm in WI, MN, or IA
The county where the farm is located
questions.explanation: The farm waiver covers the farmer, family, and employees hauling the farm's own supplies, produce, or machinery, not for hire, within 150 miles of a farm in Wisconsin, Minnesota, or Iowa. Doubles, triples, and vehicles carrying 16 or more passengers still need a CDL.

questions.q: A recreational vehicle is exempt from the CDL requirement in Wisconsin when it is not used commercially and is no longer than:
questions.explanation: A privately operated motor home, fifth wheel, or touring mobile home no longer than 45 feet, and not used commercially, does not require a CDL.

questions.q: Restriction K on a Wisconsin CDL means the driver may operate:
options: Only within the state that issued the CDL
questions.explanation: K, and restriction 51, limit the CDL to the borders of the issuing state.

questions.q: A long truck cannot make the right turn without using another lane. You should:
options: Swing wide to the left before the turn starts.
Turn wide as you complete the turn and keep the rear close to the curb.
Stop and back up until the turn fits.
Turn from the left lane so that the trailer tracks to the inside.
questions.explanation: Do not swing left at the start. A driver behind may pass on your right. Turn wide as you finish, and keep the rear near the curb. Wisconsin CDL Manual, section 2.7.6 and figure 6-5.

questions.q: On a left turn in a long combination, you should start the turn:
options: As soon as the tractor nose reaches the crosswalk.
After the tractor has reached the center of the intersection.
From the oncoming lane, to give the trailer room.
Before the stop line, to finish sooner.
questions.explanation: If you turn left too soon, offtracking can swing the left side of the vehicle into another vehicle. Reach the center first. Wisconsin CDL Manual, section 2.7.6.

questions.q: Why should you not swing left before a right turn?
options: A driver behind may think you are turning left and pass on your right.
The low air warning will come on.
The rear wheels will track well outside the curb on the turn.
questions.explanation: A following driver may pass on the right and be hit as you complete the right turn. Wisconsin CDL Manual, figure 2-13 and figure 6-6.

questions.q: In Wisconsin, what is the youngest age to drive a commercial vehicle only within the state?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin allows intrastate commercial driving at 18 years; interstate driving requires 21.
